name: Wren AI
tagline: Governed text-to-SQL and dashboards for AI agents
seoTitle: Wren AI - Open-Source Governed Text-to-SQL for Agents
metaDescription: Wren AI is an open-source generative BI engine: it grounds agent-written SQL in a governed semantic layer and context layer across 22+ data sources.
overview: Wren AI is an open-source generative BI (GenBI) engine that lets AI agents generate, deploy, and govern business intelligence — from a governed text-to-SQL answer through to a shareable dashboard — across more than 22 data sources. It is aimed at the gap between a raw LLM writing plausible-but-wrong SQL and a traditional BI tool that cannot be driven by an agent at all.

What makes the output trustworthy is the layer underneath the model: an open AI context layer plus a governed semantic layer (MDL) that supplies what a database schema alone cannot — business semantics, approved definitions, worked examples, memory, and the unstructured company knowledge that lives in docs, wikis, and chat threads. That knowledge is stored as versionable, evidence-linked files — semantic models, an instructions.md of company definitions, and a memory of queries that worked — so it is reviewable, diff-able, and kept in Git rather than locked inside a vendor UI.

Correctness is handled with concrete primitives rather than prompting alone: schema-aware retrieval, MDL planning, dry-plan validation, structured errors with hints, value profiling, row limits, and an eval runner. Wren is agent-driven by design — you install the CLI and a small discovery stub for your AI client (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Codex and others), then drive it through your existing agent. The core, SDK, and skills are Apache-2.0 licensed; row- and column-level security and access control are reserved for the Cloud and self-hosted tiers. In May 2026 the separate Wren Engine repository was merged into this one under core/, and the older Docker-based chat-first BI product was preserved on the legacy/v1 branch as Wren GenBI Classic.
features: Governed text-to-SQL grounded in a semantic layer (MDL), with schema-aware retrieval and MDL planning
An open AI context layer that captures business definitions, examples, and memory as reviewable, Git-friendly files
Dry-plan validation, row limits, and structured errors with hints to keep agent-generated SQL inside guardrails
One-command deployment of browser-side dashboards, powered by wren-core-wasm, to your own Vercel or Cloudflare Pages account
Coverage of 22+ data sources including BigQuery, Snowflake, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Amazon Redshift, and Databricks
Agent-native workflow: a ~50-line discovery stub that auto-detects Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Codex and other clients, with guides served on demand by the CLI

gettingStarted.intro: Wren is agent-driven: install the CLI, install a one-file discovery stub for your AI client, then let your agent drive the rest. Workflow guides are served from inside the CLI so they always match the installed version.

steps.heading: Install the CLI
steps.body: The core package includes DuckDB. Add per-datasource and memory extras as you need them.
steps.code:
pip install wrenai                      # core (DuckDB included)
pip install "wrenai[postgres,memory]"   # add per-datasource and memory extras as needed

steps.heading: Install the discovery stub for your AI client
steps.body: The stub teaches your agent to fetch workflow guides via wren skills get <name> and shaped prompts via wren ask.
steps.code: npx skills add Canner/WrenAI            # auto-detects Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Codex, …

steps.heading: Ask your agent to set things up
steps.body: Open your agent in a project directory and ask it to connect a database — for example, "Use Wren to set up my Postgres database." The agent runs wren skills get onboarding, checks your environment, creates a connection profile, scaffolds the project, and runs a first query.

steps.heading: Enrich the project with business context
steps.body: Ask the agent to enrich the project from your raw material. It runs wren skills get enrich-context in either grill mode (one question at a time) or auto-pilot mode (it reads <project>/raw/ and proposes), writing to MDL, instructions, queries, and memory — all reviewable and Git-friendly.

steps.heading: Ask questions and deploy a dashboard
steps.body: Ask a business question and the agent fetches MDL context, recalls similar past queries, writes governed SQL, and executes it via wren query. Ask it to turn the answer into a dashboard and it runs wren skills get genbi, builds a browser-side app from your project's context, previews it locally, and ships it to your own Vercel or Cloudflare Pages account.

useCases: Let an AI agent answer business questions in SQL without letting it guess at your schema or your metric definitions
Keep business logic — definitions, enums, units, approved joins — in a reviewable, version-controlled semantic layer instead of in prompts
Turn an ad-hoc analytical answer into a shareable dashboard deployed to your own Vercel or Cloudflare Pages account
Query across a mixed warehouse estate (BigQuery, Snowflake, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Redshift, Databricks) through one governed interface
